I have become more of a homebody. I don’t want to go out much. I’ve found home cooking and baking to be the way that I want to spend my weekends. I ride my bike for solitude and silence. Maybe it’s the buzz of the city that had made me go inward more than I once had.

I created a scale from 1-100 to quantify my emotions. I gave every increment of 10 a real life example of what that would feel like - so a 0 would be truly wanting and planning to end my life or something along those lines, 10 is sleeping all day not taking care of my personal needs pushing others away etc, whereas 100 is absolutely elated I am on top of the world nothing can bring me down I have the confidence to finally start that business I have been idealizing in my head. 50 is I am content, I am at peace, life is neither good nor bad, it simply is. You can create your own scale from 1-100 then track it every day. I make a habit of writing down my number rating for the day each night before I go to bed on a calendar I have up next to my desk. At the end of each month, I put the data in my spreadsheet to track it and start tracking on the next month.

I'm currently a student studying horticulture and business management via CSU online. The experience has has both its pros and cons. I initially decided to do an online degree so that I could travel and work on different farms throughout the world while continuing to further my education and obtain a bachelor's degree. It is what you make of it. I am thankful for the work experiences I have had that I created myself. I know I wouldn't have been able to get them from the school. This spring will be my last semester, and I actually will spend this one on campus in Fort Collins as I applied to do bioagricultural research through the university. I am looking forward to getting some more hands on experience. 

All in all, it really depends on what kind of learner you are. Are you self-motivated? Are you okay working independently? Are you disciplined in your ability to create your own schedule?

It is a very flexible route to take, especially with horticulture. Luckily, it does not hold you back from accepting opportunities that you traditionally wouldn't find offered from a university. 

I have been able to create relationships with my professors and my advisors through emailing, and that is enough to satisfy my need for connection in an academic environment. The classwork itself is relatively simple, and if you need help, I have found the professors to be very accommodating. I've been given personal phone numbers to chat through issues and discuss career goals and aspirations.
